name: EyeDB
tagline: French open-source object database with ODL schemas, OQL queries and C++/Java bindings, born at Genethon.
description: EyeDB is an object database management system that grew out of IDB, a 1992 prototype built at the Genethon genome-research laboratory in France to manage genomic data, and was rewritten and renamed EyeDB in 1994. Developed later by SYSRA, it offers a rich object model with inheritance, collections, arrays, methods, triggers and constraints; schemas are written in an ODMG-style Object Definition Language and data is queried with OQL, through native C++ and Java bindings plus Python via SWIG. It was released under the LGPL, with the OQL command-line interpreter under the GPL, and distributed on SourceForge, where the last tarball is 2.8.8 from 2010. A 2018-2019 GitHub import exists, but eyedb.org is now a parked domain and nothing has moved since.
statusNote: Last SourceForge release 2.8.8 (2010); GitHub mirror idle since 2019 and eyedb.org is parked.

license.name: GNU LGPL v2.1 (OQL interpreter under GPL)

strengths: Full ODMG-style object model: inheritance, collections, arrays, methods, triggers and constraints
Declarative OQL queries over objects, not just navigation
Open source (LGPL) with native C++ and Java bindings
weaknesses: No release since 2010 and no active maintainers
Builds target old compilers and JDKs; little surviving documentation
Tiny user community compared with relational or modern document stores
useCases: Maintaining legacy bioinformatics systems built on EyeDB
